For sparse, interrupted outlines, don't fill every gap between aligned markers by default: first check whether the markers trace an enclosing frame; if so, test filling only missing border cells and leave the interior unchanged. Implement or fix `transform(grid)` and run it against every pair received; require exact input-output matches before submitting. When entering a grid for local testing, assert its row count and every row width against the stated dimensions before calling the transform; fix transcription errors rather than submitting a partial or malformed grid.

"""Double the input grid using its clockwise rotation as the upper-right block.

The lower-left block is the upper-right block rotated 180 degrees, and the
lower-right block is the upper-right block rotated clockwise 90 degrees.
"""

def rotate_cw(grid):
    return [list(row) for row in zip(*grid[::-1])]

def transform(grid):
    n = len(grid)
    if n == 0 or any(len(row) != n for row in grid):
        raise ValueError("expected a nonempty square grid")
    top_right = rotate_cw(grid)
    bottom_left = [row[::-1] for row in top_right[::-1]]
    bottom_right = rotate_cw(top_right)
    out = [[0] * (2 * n) for _ in range(2 * n)]
    for r in range(n):
        out[r][:n] = grid[r][:]
        out[r][n:] = top_right[r]
        out[r + n][:n] = bottom_left[r]
        out[r + n][n:] = bottom_right[r]
    return out
